patch.value: Model-aware agent identity: detection resolves harness, model, and session so an agent never types an identity flag and history still records which model acted

Today src/core/shared/author.ts:detectHarnessIdentity returns only a harness slug from bounded env and argv signals, and resolveAuthorIdentity stamps author 'harness:<slug>'. The model is never captured on any path. The consequence is that the entire fleet collapses into seven author values, and history cannot answer which model wrote a decision, produced a defect, or held a claim. This item extends the resolved identity to a structured value — harness, model, model_source, session — resolved by the same pure, bounded, non-blocking detector, and threads it into the history entry as first-class provenance beside the existing author_source discriminator. Signal sources, in precedence order: an explicit PM_AGENT_MODEL override; harness-specific environment (for example ANTHROPIC_MODEL, AIDER_MODEL, CODEX_MODEL, OPENCODE_MODEL, PI_MODEL); MCP initialize clientInfo name and version for MCP-hosted callers, which is the only reliable channel when the harness runs pm out-of-process; and a bounded argv scan. Absence must be silent: an undetectable model yields provenance without a model field and must never degrade the author to unknown. Detection stays pure and bounded per the pm-z9x1r2 contract — no process traversal, no subprocess, no network — so the mutation hot path keeps its startup budget.

The public SDK resolver returns a structured identity carrying harness, model, model_source, and session alongside the existing author and source, and the CLI and MCP hosts both consume it; A mutation run under a supported harness with no PM_AUTHOR, no --author, and no author_default records the detected harness AND the detected model in its history entry; An undetectable model records provenance without a model field and never degrades the author to unknown, proven by an explicit negative test; Detection remains a pure function of caller-supplied bounded signals with no process traversal, subprocess launch, or network access, and the mutation-path latency budget is asserted in CI; MCP-hosted invocations resolve identity from the initialize clientInfo handshake when environment markers are absent; The provenance fields match the shape decided in the identity ADR exactly, and a contract test fails if the SDK emits a field the ADR does not define; Telemetry receives only the hashed identity dimensions the ADR permits, asserted by a test that inspects the exported event payload
The shortest possible pm command records the richest possible truth about who ran it
Identity is the join key for fleet analytics, per-model context profiles, claim-trust decisions, and rework attribution — none of which are computable from a seven-value author space
Every mutation on every path gains durable model provenance; agents keep typing the same short commands they type today
Any history entry can be attributed to a harness and, when knowable, to a model and session, with zero additional typing by the agent
The harness half shipped and closed on 2026-07-25; capturing the model now means one provenance migration instead of two

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Treating an observation as a fallback is a design error that keeps recurring in identity code. resolveAuthorIdentity returns early as soon as a higher-precedence branch supplies an author, so detected harness — and soon the detected model — is computed only when nothing else answered. Precedence over WHICH value is authoritative is a separate question from whether an observation is worth recording: the assertion decides the author, the observation decides the provenance, and both belong in the entry. The general rule for any future precedence chain in this codebase: resolve the authoritative value by precedence, but record every cheap observation unconditionally, and keep a discriminator saying which is which.
